security_audit.summary: All 67 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown, code examples, relative links, imports, or descriptive identity text. No external command execution, path traversal, reconnaissance, or runtime network request is present. A separate high-severity bootstrap risk allows the first authenticated user to become administrator without prior authorization.

remediation.issue: The first authenticated user automatically receives administrator privileges without a token or preconfigured identity.
remediation.suggestion: Require a deployment-configured administrator principal, signed invitation, or expiring one-time claim secret before granting the initial administrator role.

content.user_title: Build Role-Based Authorization for Caffeine AI
content.value_statement: Applications need consistent authentication and role checks across Motoko backends and React frontends. This skill provides Caffeine AI patterns for protected endpoints, profiles, login state, and migrations.
actual_capabilities: Provides Motoko setup patterns for the Caffeine AI authorization mixin.
Shows role checks for administrators, users, guests, and resource owners.
Defines protected profile endpoints for reading and saving user data.
Explains verified Internet Identity name, email, and SSO attributes.
Guides React login, logout, session restoration, and cache clearing.
Documents the authorization upgrade from version 0.x to version 1.x.
limitations: Requires Caffeine AI packages and Internet Identity conventions.
Does not secure the initial administrator bootstrap against first-login takeover.
Examples require application-specific ownership and permission decisions.
Does not deploy, compile, or test the generated application.

use_cases.title: Protect a New Caffeine AI Application
use_cases.description: Add standard roles, guarded Motoko endpoints, profiles, and Internet Identity login to a new application.

use_cases.title: Build Reliable Authentication Screens
use_cases.description: Coordinate restored sessions, login progress, profile setup, logout, and cached data in a React interface.

use_cases.title: Upgrade Authorization Dependencies
use_cases.description: Migrate authorization and core infrastructure packages while adopting the verified attribute callback.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Authorization
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Caffeine AI authorization to my application. Create administrator, user, and guest access with guarded backend endpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new application

prompt_templates.title: Implement Protected Profiles
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement user profiles with owner and administrator access. Include profile setup after login and clear cached profile data during logout.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate to Version 1
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate my existing authorization integration from version 0.x to 1.x. Update dependencies and add the optional verified attribute callback.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Authorization Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Motoko and React authorization flow. Identify missing role checks, ownership checks, session-state errors, cache leaks, and administrator bootstrap risks.

output_examples.input: Add authorization to an application where users edit their own records and administrators manage every record.
output: A role model covering administrators, users, and guests.
Backend guard placement for every protected read and write operation.
Ownership checks that permit users to edit only their own records.
Frontend behavior for login, access denial, and logout cleanup.

output_examples.input: Upgrade an existing application and store the verified email after sign-in.
output: A dependency upgrade checklist for backend and frontend packages.
A callback design that stores only verified identity attributes.
A caller-scoped method for retrieving the saved email.
Verification steps for compilation, sign-in, and restored sessions.

best_practices: Apply backend authorization checks to every protected operation.
Verify resource ownership in addition to checking broad user roles.
Clear all user-specific cached data when the identity logs out.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on hidden frontend controls as an authorization boundary.
Do not gate restored sessions on interactive login success state.
Do not expose personal records through unguarded query methods.

faq.question: Which applications fit this skill?
faq.answer: It fits Caffeine AI applications using Motoko, React, and Internet Identity.

faq.question: Does it support role-based access control?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents administrator, user, and guest roles with backend permission checks.

faq.question: Can it capture a verified email?
faq.answer: Yes. The authorization callback can receive verified Internet Identity attributes after sign-in.

faq.question: Does frontend access control protect backend data?
faq.answer: No. The backend must enforce every role and ownership rule independently.

faq.question: Can it migrate an older integration?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents package upgrades and the new authorization callback argument.

faq.question: How is the first administrator selected?
faq.answer: The documented package grants administration to the first authenticated user. Deployments should replace this with an authorized bootstrap process.
